threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for a seat on the bus before spotting the standing crowd piling in. It's like a game you haven't learned yet.
On the 59 last night, a couple argued about which chicken shop is best. Ended with one yelling, 'You wouldn’t know good wings if they slapped you!'

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I found a rogue cat lounging on my balcony, looking more at home than I ever did.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a bustling market where the scent of spices mingles with the sound of a spontaneous street concert. It’s like a sensory carnival every weekend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name every taco stand open past midnight but still complain about the new BART delays like it’s a personal offense.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo waiting for the 18 at 2 AM, tapping his watch like he had somewhere to be. Only in SF do you see a formal wear Muni wait.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that most locals avoid Plaça del Sol during the day; it’s too noisy with street performers—better to go at night.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stand at the corner of Carrer de Fraternitat, confused by which way to look for the tram.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver shouts 'next stop’ after a 30-second wait. We’re all used to just standing there.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele. Kind of magical, until the person next to me dropped their kebab.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? When I saw a street vendor juggling flaming kebabs at a corner near Tempelhofer Feld, and no one batted an eye.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do I see spontaneous dance parties break out in U-Bahn stations during strikes. It's like the city's heartbeat, refusing to stop even when transport does.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they avoid eye contact with tourists at the taco truck but still know the secret menu by heart.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni light rail today, and someone brought a dog that wouldn't stop barking. Classic SF moment—only in this city can a bark become a symphony.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the parks are for picnics, but locals know they’re just for people-watching while sipping café amb llet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the ticket machines—still fumbling with the language settings and staring blankly at the options.
